measurements.name: gf2_128_mul_karatsuba

measurements.name: gf2_128_square
measurements.note: Frobenius is GF(2)-linear. Expect exactly 0 non-free gates.

measurements.name: gf2_128_mul_const
measurements.note: Multiplication by a fixed constant is GF(2)-linear. Expect 0 non-free gates. This is why FRI folding coefficients and NTT twiddles are free in a binary field.

measurements.name: gf2_32_inv_naive_chain
measurements.note: Square-and-multiply over 2^k-2. All squarings free, so cost = (k-1) multiplications. Itoh-Tsujii reduces this to ~log2(k)+hw(k-1)-1 multiplications without changing the per-multiplication price.

measurements.name: m31_add
measurements.note: M31 = 2^31-1 modular addition. Carry chain plus a conditional subtract.

measurements.name: m31_mul
measurements.note: M31 modular multiplication with the Mersenne fold. Compare against gf2_32_mul.

measurements.name: goldilocks_mul
measurements.note: Goldilocks modular multiplication with the standard fast reduction. Compare against gf2_64_mul.

measurements.name: sha256_compression
measurements.note: One SHA-256 compression (single-block message). Validated against RustCrypto sha2. Cost is dominated by 32-bit addition carries, not by Ch/Maj.

measurements.name: blake3_compression
measurements.note: One BLAKE3 compression (single-chunk root hash). Validated against the blake3 crate. Pure ARX: every non-free gate is an addition carry.

measurements.name: keccak_f1600
measurements.note: One Keccak-f[1600] permutation via Keccak-256 of a short message. Validated against tiny-keccak. Theta/rho/pi/iota are all free; only chi costs, at exactly 1600 non-free gates per round for 24 rounds.

measurements.name: lowmc_128_m10_r20
measurements.note: LowMC. Linear layer is a full binary matrix multiply and costs zero. Non-free count is exactly 3*m*r. See the cryptanalytic caveat in gadgets/lowmc.rs before quoting this as a recommendation.

assumptions: Binary field GF(2^128) used directly as the challenge field; no extension needed.
100 queries at rate 1/2 targets roughly 100-bit soundness.
models.name: binary_field_FRI__keccak

assumptions: M31 needs a degree-4 extension for challenge soundness; extension multiplication modelled as ~4^1.585 base multiplications.
Same query count, domain and leaf shape as the binary-field row so the only variable is the field.
models.name: prime_field_FRI__m31_keccak

assumptions: Same as the keccak row but with BLAKE3 as the Merkle hash. BLAKE3 costs 163 non-free gates per byte of rate versus Keccak's 282, and BitVM already has a BLAKE3 implementation in Bitcoin Script.
models.name: binary_field_FRI__blake3

assumptions: THE CAUTIONARY ROW. This is what you get if you garble an off-the-shelf Plonky3/Stwo verifier without changing anything: Poseidon2 is designed to be cheap inside a prime-field SNARK, which makes it maximally expensive as a Boolean circuit.
Poseidon2 width 16 over M31: 8 full rounds x 16 S-boxes + 56 partial rounds x 1 S-box, x^5 = 3 multiplications each, priced at the measured m31_mul.
Hash cost is modelled, not measured. Everything it is built from is measured.
models.name: prime_field_FRI__m31_poseidon2

assumptions: SPECULATIVE. Substitutes a LowMC-based compression for Keccak to show the ceiling of what a garbling-friendly hash could buy. Not a security recommendation.
Rate assumed 16 B/compression, far worse than Keccak's 136 B, which partly cancels the per-compression saving. This is the honest version of the tradeoff.
